# @ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery Personal fork of [yuhp/opencode-models-discovery](https://github.com/yuhp/opencode-models-discovery). [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery.svg?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery) [![release](https://github.com/ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery/actions/workflows/release.yml) [![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery)](https://github.com/ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery/blob/main/LICENSE) [![OpenCode v1](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode%20v1-%3E%3D1.18.29-blueviolet)](https://opencode.ai/v1/docs) [![OpenCode v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode%20v2-%3E%3D2.2.6-blueviolet)](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/) > Discover models from OpenAI-compatible providers and add them to OpenCode automatically. This plugin queries a provider's model endpoint, applies optional filters, and injects the discovered models into OpenCode. It supports OpenCode v2 as the primary integration and keeps a separate OpenCode v1 adapter for legacy configurations. ## Features - Dynamic model discovery from `/v1/models` or a configured endpoint - Provider-level enablement, endpoint overrides, timeouts, and model filters - Optional human-friendly model names - Optional metadata enrichment for limits, reasoning, tools, attachments, structured output, and modalities - OpenCode v2 `/connect` credentials, host-managed storage, refresh commands, and model console - OpenCode v1 XDG caching, helper commands, and compatibility with Mimocode - Works with any provider that returns an OpenAI-compatible model-list response ## OpenCode v2 (recommended) OpenCode v2 uses `plugins` and `providers`. Discovery settings belong under `providers..settings.modelsDiscovery` and require `enabled: true` for that provider. ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ "@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery@2.2.0" ], "providers": { "gateway": { "name": "My Gateway", "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible", "settings": { "baseURL": "https://gateway.example.com/v1", "apiKey": "{env:GATEWAY_API_KEY}", "modelsDiscovery": { "enabled": true, "smartModelName": true, "models": { "includeBy": [{ "field": "id", "match": "^(gpt|gemini)" }] } } } } } } ``` The plugin requests `/v1/models` by default. For a provider that exposes `/models`, set `"endpoint": "/models"`. The endpoint is resolved from the provider URL's origin. You can omit `apiKey` and manage credentials with OpenCode's native `/connect` command. Resolved credentials are used in memory and are not written to configuration, caches, or logs. For the complete V2 configuration reference, see [Configuration Guide](docs/configuration.md#opencode-v2-configuration-stable-support). ### V2 commands and tools - `/models-discovery-refresh` refreshes discovered models. - `/models-discovery-console` browses providers, models, metadata, and caches. - `models_discovery_refresh` and `models_discovery_status` are available as agent tools. - Pass `rawCache: true` to `models_discovery_status` to inspect cached raw models and enrichment results. V2 caching is disabled by default and uses OpenCode's host-provided storage when enabled. After rebuilding a local plugin, restart the background service with `opencode service restart`. ## OpenCode v1 (legacy compatibility) For OpenCode v1 (`1.18.29+`), use `plugin`, `provider`, and `options`: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery@2.2.0"], "provider": { "lmstudio": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "name": "LM Studio", "options": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1", "modelsDiscovery": { "enabled": true, "smartModelName": true } } } } } ``` V1 discovery is configured per provider at `provider..options.modelsDiscovery`. V1 remains supported for compatibility, security fixes, and severe regressions; new discovery, TUI, RPC, cache, and override features target V2 first. For V1 migration, helper commands, disk caching, filters, and legacy configuration details, see: - [Configuration Guide](docs/configuration.md) - [Migrating from V1 to V2](docs/migrate-v1-to-v2.md) - [Persisted Model Discovery Cache](docs/persisted-model-discovery.md) - [Upgrade Guide](docs/upgrading.md) ## Metadata enrichment Enrichment is opt-in. Without `modelInfoFormat`, the plugin does not contact external metadata sources and leaves unknown fields unset. Supported formats include: `aiproxy`, `bifrost`, `litellm`, `lmstudio`, `llama-swap`, `models.dev`, `ollama`, `omniroute`, `openrouter`, and `vllm`. Example using `models.dev`: ```json { "modelsDiscovery": { "enabled": true, "modelInfoFormat": "models.dev" } } ``` `models.dev` uses `https://models.dev/models.json` by default and supports a custom `modelInfoEndpoint`. It also reads reasoning effort tiers from models.dev's v2 catalog (`https://models.dev/api.json`) when the default endpoint is used. Provider-specific formats read metadata from the provider's own response or endpoint. See [Model Metadata Enrichment](docs/configuration.md#model-metadata-enrichment) for format-specific paths and behavior. ## Common options All options are provider-scoped. The exact configuration path depends on the host: | Host | Configuration path | |---|---| | OpenCode v2 | `providers..settings.modelsDiscovery` | | OpenCode v1 | `provider..options.modelsDiscovery` | Frequently used options: | Option | Description | |---|---| | `enabled` | Enable or disable discovery for one provider | | `endpoint` | Model-list endpoint; defaults to `/v1/models` | | `timeoutMs` | Per-request timeout; V2 defaults to 5000 ms and V1 to 3000 ms | | `models.includeBy` / `excludeBy` | Filter raw top-level provider fields with `equals` or `match` | | `smartModelName` | Use provider-supplied human-friendly names when available | | `modelInfoFormat` | Enable provider-specific metadata enrichment | | `cache.enabled` | Enable provider model caching; disabled by default | | `persistModels.enabled` | V2: write successful model definitions to JSONC so they remain available during host reload; disabled by default | To enable model persistence on OpenCode v2, add this under `providers..settings.modelsDiscovery` in the configuration file to update: ```jsonc "persistModels": { "enabled": true, "path": "/absolute/path/to/opencode.jsonc" } ``` `path` is optional: the plugin uses `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, otherwise `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/opencode.jsonc` or the standard XDG OpenCode config directory. Use an explicit path if your file is named `opencode.json` or providers are configured in a project file. The target must already contain this provider with persistence enabled. Relative paths such as `./opencode.jsonc` resolve from the plugin location. Paths beginning with `~/`, such as `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`, expand to the current user's home directory; this also applies to environment path fallbacks. Only successful discovery updates generated entries; failed/invalid responses leave the file untouched. Existing manual models and user-edited generated models are preserved. JSONC comments are retained, writes are atomic and serialized, and unchanged inventories do not touch the file. The plugin stores ownership hashes in `persistModels.managedModels`; leave that metadata to the plugin. Persisted definitions include the upstream model ID, name, limits, tools, input/output modalities, and reasoning support; provider secrets and per-variant request settings are not copied. If you change provider accounts or endpoints, review/remove generated definitions belonging to the previous provider identity before reuse. An interrupted writer may leave a `.models-discovery.lock` beside the file; remove it only after confirming no writer is running. See the [full configuration reference](docs/configuration.md) for defaults, filter semantics, cache behavior, model assembly, and V1/V2 differences. ## Refresh behavior and verification **Known issue:** `2.1.3` still reproduced `ModelUnavailableError` in a real session during a plugin-loading window after the checks below. These checks cover refreshes of initialized plugin instances, not readiness during plugin initialization or reload. See [the investigation and regression plan](docs/issues/model-unavailable-on-reload.md). The PR branch adds opt-in `persistModels` synchronization, which passes the isolated reload/inference reproduction by giving the host model definitions in its own config. The original restored-session path remains unverified; persistence must first be enabled and complete one successful discovery. On OpenCode v2, discovery refresh keeps the current model inventory available until the new inventory is ready. If a provider request fails, the plugin retains that provider's last known inventory. These protections predate this fork's `2.1.3` release: failure retention was added in `4fcb883` on October 13, 2026, and deferred catalog reload in `7fbc9af` on October 18, 2026; both are included in upstream `v2.0.0`. Local verification of `@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery@2.1.3` on November 17, 2026 used Herdr Core terminals against the running OpenCode service: | Scenario | Concurrent terminals | Forced refreshes | |---|---:|---:| | Three different project directories | 3 | 15 | | The same project directory | 3 | 15 | Each terminal also ran two concurrent model-directory readers. Across 246 reads, the catalog remained at 249 models, and `sub2api/deepseek-v4-1-flash-261017` remained available. All 30 forced refreshes succeeded. This test did not reproduce a temporary missing model; it did not exercise inference requests during refresh, configuration reloads, service restarts, or provider failures, and does not establish that every historical `ModelUnavailableError` is fixed. ## npm release The public package is `@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery`. Version `2.2.0` uses the npm dist-tag `latest`. Use `@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery@2.2.0` to pin that release, or `@ybbapp/opencode-models-discovery@latest` to follow the stable dist-tag. npm dist-tags are separate from Git tags; this local publication did not create a Git tag. ## Documentation - [Configuration Guide](docs/configuration.md) - [Provider Compatibility](docs/providers.md) - [Connect and Auth](docs/connect-and-auth.md) - [Migrate V1 to V2](docs/migrate-v1-to-v2.md) - [Persisted Model Discovery Cache](docs/persisted-model-discovery.md) - [Upgrade Guide](docs/upgrading.md) - [Community configuration examples](docs/config_example/) ## Requirements - OpenCode with plugin support - At least one local or remote OpenAI-compatible provider - A provider model-list endpoint returning an OpenAI-compatible response For local plugin development, run `npm run compile` and reference the generated directory with `file:///absolute/path/to/opencode-models-discovery/dist`. OpenCode v2 expects a directory rather than a direct JavaScript entry file. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Please feel free to submit a pull request. Community provider examples should be added under [`docs/config_example/`](docs/config_example/) on the `community/config-examples` branch. ## License MIT ## Disclaimer This project is not built by the OpenCode team and is not affiliated with OpenCode. It is also not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by [models.dev](https://models.dev/). The optional models.dev metadata source is used only when explicitly configured.
